research_questions: How can place and relation evidence rank plausible scene completions without turning dataset frequency into a hard rule?
Which constraints must reject a candidate before seed or creativity can rank it?
How should uncertainty, embodiment, policy, and cultural applicability remain typed rather than collapsed into one compatibility score?

mechanisms.statement: Use scene-category evidence as a soft prior over otherwise eligible completions, not as a requirement that every instance of a concept must occur in its most frequent setting.
Visual Genome represents an image with object instances, object attributes, and directed relationships organized as a scene graph.
An explicit identity, action, prop, relation, environment, or prohibition in the request outranks an inferred place prior even when the inferred setting is statistically common.
Apply physical relation and declared capability gates before using context priors to rank the surviving candidates.
Keep physical feasibility, embodiment capability, user closure, safety or policy, and cultural applicability as separately inspectable gates rather than one opaque compatibility score.
When required support, contact, containment, or visibility relations cannot be established, abstain from that candidate rather than inventing the missing relation in explanatory prose.
Treat dataset co-occurrence and annotation frequency as observations about sampled images, never as proof of aesthetic quality, cultural normality, ethical acceptability, or universal prevalence.
Creativity may rerank only candidates that already pass every hard gate; it must not weaken a gate or convert a rejected candidate into an eligible one.

candidate_definitions.usc_sptg_scene_context_soft_prior: Rank eligible place and activity contexts by typed relevance while recording that the score is a prior, not a requirement.
candidate_definitions.usc_sptg_object_relation_scene_graph_rou: Route the candidate through declared object, attribute, spatial, contact, support, and containment edges before composition.
candidate_definitions.usc_sptg_explicit_identity_core_guard: Reject any inferred completion that overwrites an explicit identity-core fact, fixed slot, closed slot, or prohibition.
candidate_definitions.usc_sptg_physical_relation_gate: Reject a completion whose required support, containment, contact, scale, or line-of-effect relation is physically contradictory.
candidate_definitions.usc_sptg_capability_resource_gate: Reject a completion that requires an undeclared limb, grasp, gaze channel, support surface, occupied hand, or other unavailable resource.
candidate_definitions.usc_sptg_policy_culture_gate: Keep policy and culture-sensitive eligibility in dedicated external gates; this research record supplies routing boundaries but does not decide those domains.
candidate_definitions.usc_sptg_context_anchor_relation: Show one subject-to-place or object-to-place relation that makes the chosen context materially relevant to the event.
candidate_definitions.usc_sptg_support_relation_trace: Show one support, contact, containment, or adjacency relation whose geometry visibly satisfies the selected completion.
candidate_definitions.usc_sptg_prior_confidence_metric: Record scene-prior evidence separately from gate results and lower confidence when relation evidence is absent or ambiguous.
candidate_definitions.usc_sptg_scene_category_evidence_metric: Store source-scoped scene-category evidence, dataset identity, and uncertainty without converting category frequency into a prompt prior, norm, or hard requirement.

pixel_evidence_definitions.usc_sptg_context_anchor_relation: At least one visible subject-place or object-place edge affects stance, action, access, or consequence rather than serving as an interchangeable backdrop.
pixel_evidence_definitions.usc_sptg_support_relation_trace: The relevant contact boundary, support surface, containment boundary, or directional relation remains locatable in the target crop.

compatibility: Soft place priors are compatible with any topic route after explicit identity and slot-state preservation.
Relation graphs combine with event frames when both refer to the same actor, target, instrument, and environment nodes.
Capability and resource gates combine with human, faceless, nonhuman, quadruped, limbless, and multi-limbed declarations when no human anatomy is silently assumed.
A high-creativity route may choose an unusual eligible context after the same gates are applied.
conflicts: A frequent place label conflicts with an explicit user setting only when it is treated as a requirement instead of a prior.
A relation candidate conflicts when its contact, support, containment, scale, or line-of-effect edge is impossible in the declared scene.
A combined compatibility score conflicts with auditability when it hides whether rejection came from physics, embodiment, policy, culture, or user closure.
A scene prior conflicts with creativity control if raising creativity changes hard-gate outcomes.
counterexamples: Selecting a kitchen solely because a maid-like costume often co-occurs with domestic settings despite an explicitly requested lunar ruin.
Placing a heavy tool in a character's hand when both hands are fixed as empty or already occupied.
Calling a firearm ceremonial in prose while its scale, grip, orientation, and environment provide no such relation.
Treating a web-image category frequency as evidence that a scene is culturally universal or aesthetically preferable.
boundaries: These sources support scene categories and visible relations; they do not establish safety, legality, cultural permission, or moral acceptability.
Context frequency must not be used to infer identity, profession, nationality, class, gender, age, or intent.
The policy-culture gate is an integration boundary and requires the skill's separate policy and cultural provenance contracts.
Do not infer an invisible relation merely because a prompt explanation makes it plausible.
domain_limits: Places evidence concerns photographed environments and scene recognition, not prescriptive illustration composition.
Visual Genome concerns annotated real-world images and does not enumerate every fictional object, relation, or world rule.
Soft priors may rank scene completions only after domain-specific physical and policy gates.
Dataset frequency is not a calibrated probability for the skill's requested subculture domains.
embodiment_limits: Do not apply human hand, gaze, bipedal support, or reach assumptions to nonhuman bodies without declared capabilities.
A faceless or masked subject may satisfy attention through head, torso, appendage, or effect direction rather than eye visibility.
Quadruped, limbless, and multi-limbed subjects require separate resource claims for support and manipulation.
Unknown embodiment fails closed for a candidate that requires a specific contact mechanism.
cultural_limits: English and web-image labels can encode geography, platform, and annotator norms that are not universal.
Place-object co-occurrence must not become a costume, ethnicity, religion, or occupation stereotype.
Culture-sensitive props and rituals require explicit provenance outside this generic scene-prior layer.
User-declared cultural setting outranks inferred dataset context.
source_biases: Places is a large web-sourced scene corpus whose category boundaries and sampling distribution reflect its collection and labeling process.
Visual Genome uses crowdsourced dense English annotations and contains long-tailed, noisy, and incomplete relation labels.
Both resources emphasize photographed real-world scenes and underrepresent many fictional, nonhuman, and stylized illustration relations.
Neither source validates the runtime's authored gate taxonomy; that taxonomy remains a design inference.
runtime_implications: Resolve explicit identity core and fixed, closed, or open slots before retrieving any universal context candidate.
Materialize typed relation and resource predicates, reject failures, then apply scene priors to the surviving set.
Record every gate outcome separately and never feed rejected candidates back into ranking at higher creativity.
Require each emitted context atom to attach to the event spine through a visible relation edge.
Use deterministic seed tie-breaking only after gate and prior scores are fixed.
evaluation_implications: Mutation tests must show that explicit setting, no-prop, empty-hand, capability, and policy closures defeat a higher scene prior.
The same request and seed across creativity bands must preserve identical hard-gate outcomes.
Metadata-free review must locate the context anchor and support relation in both native and target crop views.
Unseen human, faceless, quadruped, limbless, and multi-limbed cases must either pass with declared capabilities or fail closed.
Audit reports must not describe dataset frequency as cultural universality, quality, or user preference.

title: Places: A 10 Million Image Database for Scene Recognition
authority: MIT open-access author manuscript of the IEEE TPAMI paper
limitations: The work evaluates scene recognition on photographs and does not prescribe prompt composition or illustration aesthetics.
Web-image collection and scene-category annotation do not yield universal or culture-neutral frequencies.
Scene categories can have blurry boundaries and cannot serve as hard constraints on a requested fictional scene.
The source does not support policy, safety, cultural-permission, or embodiment gates directly.

title: Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations
authority: official Visual Genome project paper page
limitations: Crowdsourced English annotations are incomplete, noisy, and long-tailed rather than an exhaustive ontology of possible relations.
The images and annotations represent sampled real-world photographs, not all fictional, nonhuman, or stylized scenes.
A labeled relation demonstrates a dataset representation, not physical feasibility in every embodiment.
Co-occurrence and label frequency do not establish cultural normality, ethics, safety, or aesthetic quality.

research_questions: Which part of creativity can semantic distance estimate, and which qualities remain outside that construct?
How should a verbal-task distance result be translated cautiously into typed image-scene distance?
How can creativity alter eligible distance distributions while leaving hard gates, candidate count, and coherence requirements unchanged?

mechanisms.statement: In the studied verbal divergent-thinking and association tasks, semantic distance can predict a meaningful portion of human novelty and creativity ratings.
Treat semantic distance as a proxy for remoteness or originality within its validated verbal tasks, not as a complete measure of usefulness, visual quality, authorship, emotion, or creativity.
SemDis compares multiple semantic models and reports that scores and data coverage depend on the semantic space, composition method, text cleaning, spelling handling, and verbal task.
Model the relationship between distance and judged creativity as potentially nonlinear: the primary study found gains up to a threshold followed by no additional judged-creativity benefit.
Do not equate the farthest available association with the most creative result; beyond the observed task-specific sweet spot, additional distance did not improve subjective ratings.

Transferring verbal semantic-distance findings to image-scene candidate selection is a design inference and must be validated with prompt and pixel holdouts rather than presented as source-supported image evidence.
Let creativity shift probability mass among near, middle, and eligible remote candidates, while keeping hard gates, user closures, safety constraints, and the bounded candidate count invariant.
Admit at most one remote high-load premise in a sparse event and require a visible causal bridge and retained core identity; otherwise reject it even at maximum creativity.
Translate model-dependent verbal semantic-distance evidence into auditable typed image-scene distance bands rather than importing one raw score or cutoff as a universal image rule.

candidate_definitions.usc_sdc_typed_distance_vector_metric: Record theme, era or technology, tone, violence, social, scale, and visual-salience distances independently instead of collapsing them into an unexplained scalar.
candidate_definitions.usc_sdc_distance_band_router: Route an eligible candidate to near, middle, or remote bands using deterministic typed rules and an auditable trace.
candidate_definitions.usc_sdc_creativity_distribution_router: Shift selection weight across eligible distance bands without increasing the number of event premises or changing gate results.
candidate_definitions.usc_sdc_hard_gate_invariance_guard: Reject any implementation in which creativity alters identity, closure, feasibility, resource, safety, policy, or cultural gate outcomes.
candidate_definitions.usc_sdc_remote_single_premise_guard: Permit no more than one remote high-semantic-load premise in the selected sparse event.
candidate_definitions.usc_sdc_visible_bridge_requirement_guard: Reject a middle or remote candidate whose relevance exists only in explanation text and lacks a visible bridge to the event spine.
candidate_definitions.usc_sdc_single_remote_premise_atom: Expose one remote but eligible object, action, or context relation that visibly changes the event while preserving the requested identity core.
candidate_definitions.usc_sdc_sweet_spot_plateau_metric: Record that human-rated creativity in the studied verbal tasks increased to a task-specific threshold and then plateaued, without transferring the numerical threshold to image generation.
candidate_definitions.usc_sdc_coherence_utility_metric: Score legible function, causal integration, and core preservation separately from semantic remoteness.
candidate_definitions.usc_sdc_verbal_semantic_distance_evidenc: Store the source-scoped verbal semantic-distance result with task, language, model, corpus, preprocessing, and human-rating context; it is not an image-quality or runtime-band score.

pixel_evidence_definitions.usc_sdc_single_remote_premise_atom: The remote premise is a locatable object, action, or environment relation connected to the actor and event in the target crop; a lore label, caption, or hidden rationale alone does not count.

compatibility: Typed semantic distance is compatible with deterministic seed selection when distance bands and gate outcomes are fixed before tie-breaking.
A remote premise is compatible with high creativity only after all hard gates pass and a causal bridge survives target-format review.
Near and middle candidates remain eligible at high creativity; creativity shifts a distribution rather than forcing maximum distance.
Distance routing combines with authorial grammar when one remote premise does not displace the primary subject-action hierarchy.
conflicts: A single lexical embedding score conflicts with the typed scene-distance contract when it hides violence, scale, technology, or salience jumps.
More candidates or more simultaneous premises conflict with the requirement that creativity change distance distribution rather than quantity.
A remote prop conflicts when it survives only because explanatory prose names a backstory.
Any creativity-dependent change to hard-gate output conflicts with gate invariance.
Maximum distance conflicts with coherence when the actor, action, target, and consequence no longer form one event.
counterexamples: Adding an unrelated machine gun to a quiet tea scene because it is lexically distant, with no visible ownership, affordance, motivation, mechanics, state change, consequence, or identity contrast.
Calling the farthest text embedding result the most creative image without evaluating visual coherence or usefulness.
Raising creativity and silently reopening a user-closed prop slot.
Adding three remote props to increase novelty while each starts a different story.
Reporting a SemDis threshold from verbal tasks as a calibrated image-quality threshold.
boundaries: The cited evidence validates verbal creativity and association tasks, not generated illustrations or image prompts.
Distance is not a proxy for safety, policy acceptability, cultural respect, emotional impact, commercial value, or authorship.
Do not import the published numerical sweet-spot threshold into a different embedding, language, task, or image domain.
Hard gates remain invariant at every creativity value.
Farther associations may plateau, become incoherent, or simply be irrelevant; far does not mean better.
domain_limits: SemDis findings apply to specific verbal divergent-thinking and association tasks using computational language models.
The nonlinear study covers alternate uses, question asking, and metaphor generation, not visual composition.
Typed image-scene distance is an authored runtime model requiring separate prompt and render qualification.
No external embedding or semantic index is required by this record; deterministic typed bands are sufficient for initial implementation.
embodiment_limits: Semantic distance cannot establish whether a body can grasp, gaze, carry, support, or operate the selected premise.
Nonhuman embodiment must pass capability and resource gates before distance ranking.
A remote action that presumes human anatomy is ineligible for an incompatible body regardless of creativity.
Faceless or nonverbal subjects require visible nonfacial bridges rather than a textual emotion rationale.
cultural_limits: Language-model distance reflects its corpora and language distributions and is not culturally neutral.
A culturally unfamiliar concept may appear distant because of corpus underrepresentation rather than creative merit.
Do not use distance to exoticize a culture or to override culture-sensitive provenance gates.
Cross-language distances are not assumed comparable without dedicated validation.
source_biases: SemDis was validated on verbal responses and depends on corpus, preprocessing, model choice, and human rating tasks.
The sweet-spot study reports a task-specific nonlinear relationship and does not establish one portable cutoff.
Both sources measure judged or modeled verbal originality more directly than usefulness, visual legibility, or image quality.
The image-scene operationalization, typed dimensions, single-remote cap, and gate invariance are design inferences.
runtime_implications: Compute gate eligibility first, then a typed distance vector for each surviving candidate.
Map the vector to near, middle, or remote bands with deterministic rules recorded in semantic_distance_trace.
Use creativity only to alter band weights, never the number of event spines, hard-gate outcomes, or user slot states.
Cap remote high-load selection at one and require a complete visible bridge before emission.
Record coherence and utility separately so a distance increase cannot mask a broken event.
evaluation_implications: Freeze identical request, format, seed, and core while varying only creativity; verify invariant gates and a bounded change in band selection.
Test that low creativity favors near low-load candidates without forbidding eligible variety, and high creativity still sometimes selects near or middle candidates.
Mutation tests must reject reopened closed slots, multiple remote premises, absent bridges, and theme-hijacking props.
Metadata-free native and crop review must identify the remote premise and why it participates in the event.
Do not claim improved image creativity from distance traces alone; prompt coherence and pixel evidence remain separate gates.

title: Automating Creativity Assessment with SemDis: An Open Platform for Computing Semantic Distance
authority: open peer-reviewed article archived by NLM PubMed Central
limitations: The five studies evaluate verbal alternate-uses and word-association responses, not visual scenes or generated images.
Semantic distance more directly estimates remoteness or originality than usefulness, coherence, aesthetics, or authorship.
Scores depend on semantic spaces, corpora, preprocessing, spelling handling, and task wording.
Image-scene distance bands, hard-gate invariance, and bridge requirements are not findings of this study.

title: A Sweet Spot for Creative Ideation: Non-Linear Associations Between Semantic Distance and Creativity
authority: official U.S. Department of Education ERIC bibliographic record for the peer-reviewed journal article, with author-linked open data and code
limitations: The reported nonlinear relationship comes from three verbal divergent-thinking tasks, not image generation or illustration review.
The observed threshold is specific to the study's semantic-distance implementation and should not be transferred numerically.
The result shows a plateau in judged creativity after a threshold, not that every distant response becomes incoherent.
The study does not validate hard gates, remote-premise caps, causal bridges, or typed image-distance dimensions.

research_questions: How can an unusual prop or action be connected to one event through explicit participant and relation roles?
Which bridge classes can be made observable in a still image without relying on lore prose?
What must fail closed when a prompt explains relevance but the target crop contains no bridge evidence?

mechanisms.statement: Represent an event through explicit participant roles and relations so an added object or action has a typed place in the event rather than an unstructured topical association.
Separate the event visibly depicted in the current frame from abductive hypotheses about what happened before, what may happen after, and what a person may intend.

In activity-centric images, jointly predicting the activity and its participant roles can outperform treating object and activity recognition as independent tasks, supporting event-level representation.
Keep image-grounded present-event roles separately traceable from plausible before, after, and intent inferences so an inferred dynamic context is never mistaken for a visibly depicted fact.
Use exactly these operational bridge types for this layer: affordance, motivation, mechanics, ownership, state_change, consequence, and identity_contrast.

A motivation bridge must be realized as an observable goal vector such as approach, avoidance, reaching, guarded possession, gaze or appendage direction, or a target response; an asserted inner motive is insufficient.
Reject a bridge that exists only in prompt explanation, metadata, caption, or lore when no corresponding contact, relation, state difference, consequence, or contrast is visible in the target crop.
An identity-contrast bridge requires a visible juxtaposition between a preserved identity cue and the remote premise, plus one event relation; a surprising noun pair alone does not qualify.

Do not let a plausible before, after, or intent rationale convert an ungrounded or independently ineligible present-event role into a visibly depicted fact; bridge resolution occurs only after hard gates.

candidate_definitions.usc_cbg_event_frame_router: Assign actor, action, target, instrument, recipient, initial state, result, and environment roles before selecting a bridge.
candidate_definitions.usc_cbg_affordance_bridge_atom: Show the actor using or preparing to use a physically eligible action possibility of the premise through a locatable contact or approach relation.
candidate_definitions.usc_cbg_motivation_bridge_atom: Show an observable goal vector toward or away from the premise without claiming an unobservable inner state.
candidate_definitions.usc_cbg_mechanics_bridge_atom: Show how force, support, attachment, transmission, loading, or operation connects the premise to the event.
candidate_definitions.usc_cbg_ownership_bridge_atom: Show possession or custody through fitted wear, repeated repair, personalized adaptation, guarded transfer, storage, or another visible relation; do not infer legal ownership.
candidate_definitions.usc_cbg_state_change_bridge_atom: Show a before-to-after difference in the actor, object, or environment caused by interaction with the premise.
candidate_definitions.usc_cbg_consequence_bridge_atom: Show residue, displacement, damage, repair, recoil response, witness response, or system response attributable to the premise's event role.
candidate_definitions.usc_cbg_identity_contrast_bridge_atom: Juxtapose one preserved identity cue with the remote premise and connect them through the same visible event.
candidate_definitions.usc_cbg_pixel_grounded_bridge_guard: Reject any selected bridge lacking its required visible evidence in the target format and crop.
candidate_definitions.usc_cbg_orphan_novelty_guard: Reject every noncore premise with no typed event edge or with an edge that starts a competing event spine.
candidate_definitions.usc_cbg_bridge_coverage_metric: Measure whether every selected noncore premise has at least one typed bridge and whether all required bridge evidence survives composition.
candidate_definitions.usc_cbg_dynamic_context_hypothesis_route: Route at most one plausible before, after, or intent proposition as a hypothesis that can suggest a bridge but cannot count as current-frame evidence.
candidate_definitions.usc_cbg_grounded_present_inference_separ: Keep image-grounded present-event roles distinct from inferred dynamic context and reject any inference promoted to a visible fact without a corresponding visual atom.

pixel_evidence_definitions.usc_cbg_affordance_bridge_atom: A specific contact, reach, grasp, support, or use relation between actor and premise is locatable.
pixel_evidence_definitions.usc_cbg_motivation_bridge_atom: A directional body, head, gaze-equivalent, reach, approach, avoidance, defense, or recipient response points to a visible goal.
pixel_evidence_definitions.usc_cbg_mechanics_bridge_atom: The relevant load path, attachment, support, control surface, force direction, or operational relation is spatially coherent.
pixel_evidence_definitions.usc_cbg_ownership_bridge_atom: Fitted adaptation, use wear, repeated repair, guarded storage, custody transfer, or another visible possession relation links premise and subject.
pixel_evidence_definitions.usc_cbg_state_change_bridge_atom: The changed region and its causal contact or event relation can both be located without reading metadata.
pixel_evidence_definitions.usc_cbg_consequence_bridge_atom: At least one residue or response has a clear spatial and directional relation to the event rather than generic spectacle.
pixel_evidence_definitions.usc_cbg_identity_contrast_bridge_atom: The preserved identity cue and the remote premise are simultaneously visible and participate in one actor-action-target relation.

compatibility: Affordance and mechanics bridges combine when the same contact both permits and transmits an action.
Ownership and state-change bridges combine when use history or repair visibly explains the present state.
Motivation and consequence bridges combine when a visible goal vector and its result remain within one event spine.
Identity contrast combines with exactly one functional bridge so surprise does not replace causality.
Apple, hammer, and firearm candidates may share the global pool only after their different load, risk, capability, and policy gates pass.
conflicts: A prompt-only backstory conflicts with the pixel-grounded bridge guard.
Object presence without interaction, state, consequence, custody, or contrast conflicts with bridge completeness.
Two remote premises with separate causal chains conflict with the single-event contract.
A motivation label conflicts when no observable goal vector exists or when it asserts a private mental state from appearance alone.
A bridge conflicts with any failed hard gate and cannot be used as an exception.
counterexamples: A machine gun appears beside a maid character while the prompt calls it an heirloom, but no contact, custody marker, action, state, or consequence is visible.
A hammer is held near a broken halo but its orientation, contact, and repaired area do not align.
An apple is described as forbidden lore while it is only decorative background clutter with no actor relation.
A character looks surprised next to a remote prop, but the surprise has no target and the prop starts no event.
A caption explains that a nonhuman creature owns a tool even though its declared body cannot manipulate or carry it.
boundaries: imSitu grounds activities, participants, and roles in activity-centric images but does not guarantee that every role or bridge remains visible in a target crop.
VisualCOMET models plausible before, after, and intent inferences with person grounding; its generated textual inferences are not themselves pixel evidence.
Do not infer inner motivation, legal ownership, moral alignment, profession, or identity from a bridge cue.
Dangerous props require separate safety and policy gates; this grammar does not provide operational weapon instructions.
A causal explanation is not pixel evidence unless its observable carrier survives the required crop.
domain_limits: The grammar targets sparse still-image event composition, not multi-step procedural instruction or complete narrative causality.
imSitu is an activity-centric still-image situation benchmark and VisualCOMET is a textual visual-commonsense inference benchmark; the seven bridge types are an authored transfer.
Abstract, dreamlike, or symbolic requests may use identity contrast but still require a visible relational carrier.
Safety, legal, medical, and culture-sensitive eligibility remain outside the bridge resolver.
embodiment_limits: Both source datasets are strongly human-centered; nonhuman subjects require declared manipulation, support, perception, and expression capabilities.
A bridge cannot assume hands, forward-facing eyes, bipedal stance, or human-scale tools.
Faceless subjects may use head, torso, appendage, light, or environmental direction for motivation evidence.
Unknown grasp, support, or control capability fails closed for affordance and mechanics bridges.
cultural_limits: imSitu's English situation-role vocabulary and VisualCOMET's English commonsense annotations do not exhaust culture-specific event construals.
Possession, gift, ritual, threat, and status cues can be culture-dependent and must not be universalized.
Identity contrast must not rely on ethnic, religious, gender, class, disability, or nationality stereotypes.
A culturally specific bridge requires scoped provenance beyond this universal layer.
source_biases: imSitu emphasizes activity-centric images and annotated verb-role-noun structures, so its labels and image distribution do not cover every quiet, symbolic, fictional, or nonhuman scene.
VisualCOMET uses movie-derived still images and English crowdsourced before, after, and intent descriptions that are plausible inferences rather than observed causal facts.
VisualCOMET person grounding does not by itself ground props, contact geometry, state boundaries, or consequences.
Neither source validates the seven bridge types, one-event limit, hard-gate contract, prompt-only rejection rule, or target-crop pixel requirements directly.
runtime_implications: Create one image-grounded present-event frame and store any before, after, or intent proposition in a separate dynamic-context hypothesis field.
Choose one primary bridge type and at most one supporting bridge type for a remote premise.
Emit bridge-specific visual atoms, then run grounded-present separation, pixel-grounded, and orphan-novelty guards before composition.
Reject any bridge represented only by rationale text or metadata and preserve the exact rejection reason.
Run identity, closure, physical, capability, resource, safety, policy, and cultural gates before bridge resolution.
evaluation_implications: Mutation tests must delete each bridge carrier in turn and verify that a remote premise then fails closed.
Prompt audit must distinguish object presence from contact, use, state, custody, consequence, and contrast evidence.
Metadata-free native and target-crop review must identify the actor, premise, bridge type, and event consequence.
A hypothesis-promotion mutation must fail when a plausible before, after, or intent sentence lacks a present-frame visual carrier.
Test apple, hammer, and firearm examples at matched core and seed to verify increasing load changes gates and bridge burden rather than universal-pool membership.
Include faceless and nonhuman holdouts to prove that human hand and gaze assumptions are not silently required.

title: Situation Recognition: Visual Semantic Role Labeling for Image Understanding
authority: Computer Vision Foundation open-access accepted CVPR paper
limitations: The benchmark focuses on activity-centric still images and does not represent every quiet, symbolic, fictional, or nonhuman scene.
Situation roles ground activity participants but do not prove causal history, inner intent, ownership, state transition, or consequence.
Its English verb-role-noun inventory and annotated image distribution are not culturally or ontologically exhaustive.
The paper does not validate the seven bridge types, hard gates, prompt-only rejection, or target-crop pixel criteria.

title: VisualCOMET: Reasoning about the Dynamic Context of a Still Image
authority: European Computer Vision Association official accepted ECCV paper page
limitations: Before, after, and intent descriptions are plausible textual commonsense inferences, not directly observed pixel facts or established causal truth.
The source is person-centered and movie-derived, so it does not establish nonhuman embodiment, generic prop affordance, or cross-cultural universality.
Person co-reference grounding does not by itself ground prop contact, force paths, ownership, state boundaries, or consequences.
The paper does not validate the seven bridge types, hard gates, prompt-only rejection, or target-crop pixel criteria.

research_questions: When should the environment function as an action affordance, and when should it function as a residue or response proving consequence?
How can target-format and crop survival be tested separately from the total salience-load budget?
How can anti-repetition be measured across selections without being confused with within-image visual salience?

mechanisms.statement: Use transformed object or material states as evidence of physical or functional difference rather than treating state adjectives as decorative texture.
Require noun-state compatibility because the source dataset shows that each noun supports only a small subset of the total state vocabulary rather than every adjective combining freely.
Every selected environment atom must either enable or constrain the action as an affordance, or remain as a residue or response attributable to the action; generic atmosphere alone does not qualify.
Evaluate target crops as transformations that can remove distracting content but can also change the retained content and composition, rather than assuming a strong full frame survives automatically.
Attach each environment affordance or residue to the same actor-action-target event through contact, access, force, state, spatial, or response evidence.
Measure whether required evidence survives each target crop separately from how much visual-attention load the selected atoms compete for inside that crop.
Track anti-repetition from selection history across outputs, not from a single image's salience map; repeated exposure and within-frame visual dominance are different metrics.
Reject a candidate that is legible only in the full frame when the required card, cover, banner, or thumbnail crop removes its event edge or state boundary.
A residue, displacement, damage, repair, witness response, or system response counts only when its location, direction, or contact makes the selected event a plausible specific cause.

candidate_definitions.usc_ecs_environment_role_router: Choose exactly one primary environment role, action_affordance or consequence_residue, and allow one lower-load supporting response only when it shares the event edge.
candidate_definitions.usc_ecs_environment_affordance_atom: Show a surface, opening, support, obstacle, current, weather condition, machine state, or spatial access relation that enables or constrains the action.
candidate_definitions.usc_ecs_material_residue_atom: Show dust, droplets, fragments, scorch, frost, displaced fabric, shed material, or another bounded residue whose pattern follows the event.
candidate_definitions.usc_ecs_displacement_damage_repair_atom: Show one object or environment region displaced, damaged, opened, repaired, depleted, filled, bent, folded, aged, or otherwise visibly transformed by the event.
candidate_definitions.usc_ecs_witness_or_system_response_atom: Show a nearby witness, alarm, indicator, mechanism, animal, light, fluid, or environmental system responding to the same event without relying on readable text.
candidate_definitions.usc_ecs_event_edge_guard: Reject an environment atom that lacks a typed affordance or causal-result edge to the selected event spine.
candidate_definitions.usc_ecs_crop_safe_evidence_guard: Reject an atom whose contact, state boundary, directional pattern, or response carrier is removed or made ambiguous in any required target crop.
candidate_definitions.usc_ecs_salience_load_metric: Estimate within-frame competition from size, contrast, sharpness, motion cue, violence, foreground overlap, and semantic load.
candidate_definitions.usc_ecs_crop_survival_metric: Record whether each required atom and its event edge remain locatable at every specified aspect ratio and thumbnail size.
candidate_definitions.usc_ecs_exposure_repetition_metric: Track candidate and family exposure across prior selections independently of current-frame salience.

pixel_evidence_definitions.usc_ecs_environment_affordance_atom: The enabling or constraining surface, opening, support, obstacle, condition, or access path and its relation to the actor are both visible in the target crop.
pixel_evidence_definitions.usc_ecs_material_residue_atom: Residue has a bounded origin, direction, distribution, or contact pattern attributable to the event rather than uniform atmospheric noise.
pixel_evidence_definitions.usc_ecs_displacement_damage_repair_atom: A clear state or material boundary identifies the changed region, and a nearby actor, instrument, force direction, or aftermath relation identifies the event.
pixel_evidence_definitions.usc_ecs_witness_or_system_response_atom: The responding carrier and its directional, state, light, posture, or mechanical change are visible without requiring readable labels.

compatibility: An environment affordance combines with a consequence residue when both share one action and do not create competing focal events.
Material residue combines with state change when the residue originates at the changed boundary.
Crop survival combines with salience budgeting when each is reported separately and failure in either can reject the candidate.
Anti-repetition combines with deterministic selection only as a history-aware ranking term after hard gates.
A low-load environment response may support a remote prop bridge without becoming a second remote premise.
conflicts: Generic fog, sparks, debris, or glow conflicts with the event-edge guard when it has no attributable source or action relation.
A full-frame-only clue conflicts with a required crop-safe contract.
Several high-contrast residues conflict with the salience budget when they overpower core identity or contact evidence.
Using a salience score as an anti-repetition measure conflicts with the separation between within-image attention and cross-output exposure.
A state adjective conflicts when the object does not afford that state or no state boundary is visible.
counterexamples: Random sparks surround a static character although no contact, mechanism, damage, or system response explains them.
A repaired halo is named in the prompt but the repaired joint is outside the card crop.
A residue covers the whole frame uniformly and cannot be traced to the actor, prop, or target.
The same dramatic debris family is selected in every output because high salience is mistaken for diversity.
An environment is labeled dangerous from color alone without an observable affordance or consequence.
boundaries: MIT States provides object-state and transformation evidence, not direct causal proof from a single still image.
The crop study concerns photographic crops and does not establish universal illustration aesthetics or viewer preference.
Salience load is not the same as importance, quality, memorability, engagement, or anti-repetition.
Anti-repetition is a runtime selection-history property and has no single-image pixel-evidence claim.
Do not infer intent, blame, identity, or diagnosis from environmental residue or damage.
domain_limits: The layer targets still-image prompts with one event spine and cannot reconstruct a full temporal cause from residue alone.
State compatibility learned from web images does not enumerate every fictional material or magic-system transformation.
Crop rules must be instantiated for the requested cover, card, banner, vertical, or thumbnail format rather than one universal safe area.
Operationally dangerous, medical, legal, and policy-sensitive consequences remain governed by separate gates.
embodiment_limits: An environment affordance exists relative to the declared actor's size, locomotion, manipulation, perception, and support capabilities.
Do not assume a human reach, hand contact, standing height, or gaze channel for a nonhuman subject.
A faceless subject may connect to the environment through posture, appendage direction, contact, light, or system response.
Unknown capability fails closed when the environment role requires a specific contact or access path.
cultural_limits: Damage, repair, cleanliness, ownership, sacredness, alarm, and residue meanings can be culturally or contextually specific.
Do not treat web-image state frequency as a universal norm of maintenance, danger, purity, or value.
Culture-specific environmental signs require scoped provenance and cannot depend on generated readable text.
Cropping preferences learned from expert photographs are not assumed universal across markets or formats.
source_biases: MIT States contains 63,440 web images, 245 nouns, and 115 adjectives, with curated and uneven noun-state compatibility rather than an exhaustive transformation ontology.
The crop study learns from expert before-and-after photographic crops and may encode genre, dataset, and professional-composition preferences.
Neither source directly validates subculture illustration, generated-image pixel evidence, salience budgets, or selection-history diversity.
Environment-role typing, causal attribution, crop-safe guards, and anti-repetition separation are authored design inferences.
runtime_implications: Route each environment candidate as action_affordance or consequence_residue before adding it to the event.
Require a typed event edge and noun-state or capability compatibility before salience ranking.
Compute crop survival for every required aspect ratio and thumbnail, then compute within-frame salience load as a separate value.
Track family exposure across prior selections in an anti-repetition metric that never substitutes for current pixel evidence.
Drop any full-frame-only or unattributable atom before prompt composition and record the rejection reason.
evaluation_implications: Mutation tests must remove the event edge, state boundary, residue direction, or response carrier and cause the environment atom to fail.
Review native, every required crop, and thumbnail separately; passing the full frame cannot compensate for a failed target crop.
Measure salience-load collisions against core identity, action contact, expression channel, and primary prop role.
Run repeated deterministic selections across candidate families to test exposure diversity without changing hard-gate outcomes.
Metadata-free reviewers must classify each retained environment atom as action affordance or attributable residue and locate its event edge.

title: Discovering States and Transformations in Image Collections
authority: official MIT author project page for the CVPR paper and dataset
limitations: The dataset represents object, scene, and material states in still images and does not by itself establish the cause of a transformation.
Only a subset of nouns and adjectives is included, with web-image and annotation bias.
Noun-state compatibility does not establish safety, policy eligibility, cultural meaning, or nonhuman capability.
The source does not validate crop survival, salience budgeting, anti-repetition, or generated illustration quality.

title: Learning the Change for Automatic Image Cropping
authority: Computer Vision Foundation open-access accepted CVPR paper
limitations: The study evaluates photographic crops and does not define universal illustration composition or viewer attention.
Expert before-and-after crops can encode dataset, genre, and professional preference biases.
A learned crop score does not prove narrative causality, semantic importance, diversity, or anti-repetition.
The source does not specify the runtime's event-edge, consequence-attribution, or multi-format crop-safe guards.
